answer: The A2 generator (a2-ssot-generator 1.0.0 at command-center/p2-wave/probes/ARC-0010/generator.py) is a pure function of registry bytes: two generate() runs over command-center/p2-wave/probes/ARC-0010/registry.json produced 10 byte-identical files. Injecting datetime.now() into provenance() turns that determinism test red; dropping sort_keys and reversing dict key order on the second run also turns it red. CRLF working-tree bytes versus LF blob bytes from git cat-file -p yield the same PASS verdict after LF normalisation (blob_crlf=0 worktree_crlf=9; raw bytes differ). git archive is not the evidence route. Naive classify() reports MISSING_PROVENANCE on CRLF markdown because HEADER_RE requires a bare LF; the suite LF-normalises before parse so both trees stay CLEAN and a content mutant goes TAMPERED on both. Independent reviewer: an import-time UUID in provenance stays green under same-process two-run and is therefore a mutation this suite would NOT catch. No A2 rebuild. SUCCESS:ARC-0015

uncaught_mutation.injection: GENERATOR_RUN_ID = str(uuid.uuid4()) at module import (or once per process), then copied into every provenance header
uncaught_mutation.title: Process-lifetime identifier assigned once per import
uncaught_mutation.why_suite_misses_it: The catalog mutation control compares two generate() calls in one process. An import-time UUID is constant for that process, so two_run_identical stays green even though a second process would differ. Catching it needs a cross-process replay, which this suite does not run.
